title: rootless --userns=nomap adds gid 0 to the container's supplementary groups, but not podman exec's
body:
### Issue Description

With `--userns=nomap` and a non-root `--user`, the container's process gets supplementary gid 0,
which it never asked for. The generated OCI spec has `"additionalGids": [0, 1000]`, where without
`nomap` it has `[1000]`. Processes started with `podman exec` in the same container get `1000`
only.

So a container's own processes and exec'd ones get different permissions. I hit this with the
acme.sh image, whose `/acmebin` is `drwx---rwx root:root`: its cron job, a child of the
container's own process, got `Permission denied` on every run for three weeks, while its health
check and every `podman exec` worked. The kernel checks a member of a file's group against the
group bits, which are empty there.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

```
podman run --rm --user 1000:1000 alpine grep Groups /proc/self/status
podman run --rm --userns=nomap --user 1000:1000 alpine grep Groups /proc/self/status
podman run -d --name t --userns=nomap --user 1000:1000 alpine sleep 300
podman exec t grep Groups /proc/self/status
jq -c .process.user "$(podman inspect t --format '{{.StaticDir}}')/config.json"
```

### Describe the results you received

```
Groups:	1000
Groups:	0 1000
Groups:	1000
{"uid":1000,"gid":1000,"umask":18,"additionalGids":[0,1000]}
```

The same with every `--user` form (`1000`, `1000:1000`, a name, `name:group`) and with
`--group-add 1000`. `--userns=auto` and `--userns=keep-id` give `1000` only.

### Describe the results you expected

`Groups: 1000`, as without `nomap`, and the same groups for the container's process and for
`podman exec`.

### podman info output

```
Reproduced, rootless, on:
podman 6.1.3, crun 1.30.1, Fedora 45, kernel 7.3.3-300.fc45
podman 5.8.9, crun 1.30,   Fedora 44, kernel 7.3.3-200.fc44
Also seen, through the same acme.sh failure, on podman 5.8.2, crun 1.30.1, AlmaLinux 10.
```

### Podman in a container

No

### Privileged Or Rootless

Rootless

### Upstream Latest Release

No: 6.1.3. 6.2.0's release notes mention no fix for this.

### Additional environment details

Under `nomap`, gid 0 inside is the first subordinate gid on the host, the group that owns the
image files of every `nomap` container, so the extra group is real membership.

### Additional information

I couldn't find where the 0 comes from. `libpod/container_internal_common.go` adds the user's
primary gid and the `--group-add` groups, and skips the `/etc/group` lookup for a `uid:gid`
`--user`.
